title: The Promise of Sandpiper Point
premise: Dominic Montrose, a celebrated wedding planner who quietly stopped believing in love after his own engagement collapsed, is hired to orchestrate a destination wedding at Sandpiper Point, a coastal orchard whose deed inexplicably bears two names: his late mother's and that of Marisol Vega, the estranged heir who grew up there. As legal tangles force them into uneasy partnership, Dominic discovers his mother and Marisol's grandmother once made a promise to each other that both families spent decades avoiding, and Marisol must decide whether to sell the dying orchard to developers or fight for it. When the wedding itself threatens to erase everything Marisol loves, Dominic risks the career that saved him by walking away from the biggest event of his life. In the end, they honor the old promise on their own terms—marrying the orchard back to life rather than each other for show—and choose each other freely as the first blossoms return.
about_author: Elodie Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former estate lawyer who traded contract disputes for love stories set against crumbling family legacies. She writes from a converted barn on the northern coast, where she keeps a stubborn apple tree alive out of principle.

chapters.title: The Muscle That Forgets
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He runs a flawless society wedding in Manhattan with surgical detachment, privately viewing the heart as a trainable muscle. A call offers him the commission of a lifetime: a celebrity wedding at Sandpiper Point. Beat: polished control masking a man who has stopped feeling anything at weddings but relief.

chapters.title: A Deed With Two Names
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She returns to the neglected orchard after her grandmother's funeral, intending a quick sale, and discovers the deed lists a stranger's name alongside her family's: Montrose. Beat: grief sharpened into suspicion; she refuses to be pushed off her own ground.

chapters.title: Arrival at Sandpiper Point
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He arrives to scout the venue and finds the 'owner' barricading the gate. Their first collision is over a fallen pear tree blocking the drive. Beat: instant antagonism laced with an unwilling spark of recognition—he knows the name Montrose shouldn't be on that paper either.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Forced into negotiation, they strike a brittle deal: the wedding proceeds, proceeds split, ownership resolved afterward. Marisol sets rules; Dominic agrees too easily, which unsettles her. Beat: wary truce, two people circling the same secret.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Kept
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Sorting the farmhouse, she finds letters between her grandmother and a woman named Celeste Montrose—promises about the land, a shared plan never fulfilled. Beat: the past cracks open; Marisol realizes the deed is a message, not a mistake.

chapters.title: The Client Who Wants Everything
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. His celebrity client demands the orchard's heritage trees be removed for a glass pavilion. Dominic hesitates for the first time in years, then signs off anyway. Beat: the price of survival—he has always chosen the career, and hates how easily he does it again.

chapters.title: Pruning Season
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She begins restoring a block of trees the client wants gone, working at dawn. Dominic catches her and, instead of reporting it, picks up shears. Beat: complicity blooms; hands in the same soil make arguing harder.

chapters.title: Celeste and Rosa
chapters.summary: Dual timeline via letters, framed by both POVs. The letters reveal Celeste (Dominic's mother) and Rosa (Marisol's grandmother) promised to save the orchard together before a bitter falling-out scattered them. Beat: the younger pair sees their own conflict mirrored and misread by the older one.

chapters.title: Rain on the Pavilion Glass
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A storm wrecks half the wedding setup; Marisol's knowledge of the land saves what logistics couldn't. Working through the night, they talk honestly for the first time—his broken engagement, her years away. Beat: intimacy arrives sideways, through crisis.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Developers approach her directly with a sum that would erase her debts, contingent on the wedding going smoothly and the Montrose claim being extinguished. Beat: temptation with teeth—the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Muscle Memory
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. His ex-fiancée appears as a wedding vendor, and old wounds reopen; he realizes he built his entire career as armor. Marisol witnesses a private moment of his unraveling. Beat: vulnerability exchanged without permission.

chapters.title: First Blossom
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. An out-of-season tree blossoms on the block they saved together. They share a kiss neither planned, then retreat—Dominic to his checklist, Marisol to the developer's number. Beat: hope and fear arriving in the same breath.

chapters.title: Paper Cuts
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Dominic's firm discovers his conflict of interest and threatens removal from the project; Marisol learns he initially advised the client the orchard was 'easily acquired.' Beat: trust fractures on technicalities, both partly guilty.

chapters.title: The Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Wedding rehearsal exposes the couple's own hollow marriage-of-convenience, mirroring his cynicism back at him. Marisol watches him perform belief beautifully and wonders which of them is lying. Beat: disillusionment deepening before the turn.

chapters.title: What the Deed Meant
chapters.summary: Both POVs. They finally read the last letter together: Celeste and Rosa put both names on the deed deliberately, betting their grandchildren would finish what they started—or forgive each other trying. Beat: revelation reframes everything; the inheritance is the reconciliation, not the land.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Two days before the wedding, the developer forces her hand: sign tonight or lose the offer forever. Dominic, discovering the deadline, must choose between smoothing the event and backing her fight. Beat: rising dread, loyalties under load.

chapters.title: The Walkout
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. On the wedding morning, the client orders bulldozers into the heritage block as a 'surprise feature.' Dominic walks out mid-event, torching his reputation, and stands with Marisol between the machines and the trees. Beat: climax of character—the muscle finally trained toward courage.

chapters.title: Vows, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Chaos erupts; the bride, moved by the standoff, publicly calls off her own sham wedding and sides with them. The developer withdraws amid scandal. Beat: catharsis—the false promise collapses so a true one can stand.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Fallout: Dominic blacklisted, Marisol solvent only through a community co-op plan they sketch at the kitchen table. Grief for what each lost mixes with unexpected lightness. Beat: the quiet morning after, testing whether the choice holds.

chapters.title: The Promise, Rewritten
chapters.summary: Both POVs. They amend the deed themselves—not dissolving it, but founding the Sandpiper Trust in Celeste and Rosa's names, the orchard held in common. Beat: resolution of theme; memory honored by action, identity rebuilt on chosen ground.

chapters.title: A Wedding Worth Believing
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Months later, the town throws a harvest festival-wedding for the orchard's rebirth, and Marisol asks Dominic to plan it—not as armor, but as a gift. He says yes with his whole chest. Beat: joy earned; the planner believes again.

chapters.title: Sandpiper Point, Spring
chapters.summary: Shared final chapter, alternating voices. Under full blossom, Dominic proposes with a ring hidden in a grafting knife; Marisol answers by handing him pruning shears—stay and grow something. Epilogue image: two names on the deed, two names on a new promise. Beat: love as cultivation, not containment.
